metadata.title: Results from TALIS 2024: United Arab Emirates

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD TALIS 2024 note reports descriptive survey results based on self-reported questionnaires from lower secondary teachers and principals collected in 2024. The note does not provide microdata-processing details (e.g., which TALIS sampling weights or replicate weights were applied) and does not describe any analytic subsample restrictions beyond focusing on statistically significant differences/changes. Because this is a results note rather than a methodological analysis paper, the document should be interpreted as using the OECD TALIS 2024 database tables as published, which are produced under TALIS’s complex survey design. Analysts using TALIS microdata should apply the official TALIS sampling weights and replicate weights recommended for TALIS 2024 when estimating percentages and differences, and should not treat the figures as unweighted convenience-sample estimates.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a TALIS 2024 results note based on self-reported questionnaire items (e.g., teachers’ perceptions, experiences, and attitudes), not on cognitive achievement scores that use plausible values. As a result, plausible-value generation/combining is not applicable to the reported outcomes. The note also does not describe any missing-data handling procedure because it relies on OECD-published database tables rather than reporting an original model-estimation workflow.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The note reports findings for the United Arab Emirates from TALIS 2024 lower secondary teachers and principals, and compares them to an OECD average and other participating countries/territories. It does not specify an analytic subsample restriction (e.g., grade band beyond lower secondary, school type, or item-completion thresholds) and instead states that it comments only on statistically significant differences or changes using OECD TALIS 2024 database tables.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD TALIS 2024 results note summarizes self-reported characteristics and perceptions of lower secondary teachers and principals in the United Arab Emirates, using OECD TALIS 2024 database tables. The note reports percentages and averages (e.g., teacher age distribution, gender composition, experience profiles, perceived ability to adapt teaching to diversity, special education needs context, and social-emotional learning confidence) and highlights only statistically significant differences or changes relative to the OECD average. It also reports technology-related items (e.g., hybrid/online teaching in the last month and reported AI use in the prior 12 months) and teacher learning opportunities (initial teacher education preparation, induction/mentoring, and continuous professional learning impacts, needs, and barriers). Because TALIS is based on self-reports, the note cautions that cross-country comparisons reflect perceptions shaped by social and cultural context. No student-level predictive modeling, plausible values, or missing-data handling strategy is described in this note; it is intended for policy interpretation of descriptive patterns rather than causal inference.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a descriptive OECD TALIS 2024 results note rather than an empirical ML/predictive study. Consequently, there is no reported student-level analytic sample size, no model-estimation pipeline, no ML algorithms, and no plausible-values or missing-data handling strategy to extract. The document’s focus is on presenting OECD TALIS 2024 database table outputs (percentages/means and statistically significant differences), so many fields required for ML-method extraction are inherently sparse by design.
